summary: At 2,959 square miles, Tehama County is larger than the entire state of Delaware yet holds fewer than 65,000 people — a density of just 22 per square mile that translates to vast stretches of oak-studded rangeland, volcanic foothill terrain rising toward Lassen Peak to the east, and the Sacramento River threading through the valley floor near Red Bluff, the county seat. That river corridor and the surrounding Sacramento Valley give the landscape an open-sky, agricultural-horizon quality, with walnut and olive orchards, cattle ranches, and alfalfa fields defining much of the economic base alongside healthcare and public-sector employment. A median home value around $315,600 against a median household income of roughly $61,800 yields a price-to-income ratio near 5.1 — meaningfully more accessible than California's coastal counties, though a 15.4% poverty rate signals that affordability is relative and the local wage structure is modest. Summers are hot and sun-drenched — averaging 71°F highs with nine hours of daily sunshine — while winters cool into the 40s and 50s, keeping the landscape green along the river. The Sacramento River Trail near Red Bluff offers accessible walking and cycling, but day-to-day life is firmly car-dependent across a landscape where the nearest major metro, Redding, sits about 30 miles north. Tehama is a place where the land itself is the main attraction and the tradeoff is isolation — lots of sky, limited infrastructure.
